attempted_claim: For n>=3, is every complete graphical translator in R^{n+1} convex? In particular, are the complete translators u:Omega->R constructed by Hoffman-Ilmanen-Martin-White with prescribed tip Hessian D^2u(0)=diag(-k_1,..., -k_n), sum k_i=1, k_i>=0 (Theorem 8.1), and the slab Delta-wings u:R^n x (-b,b)->R, b>pi/2 (Theorem 11.1), all convex, or does there exist a complete nonconvex translating graph in higher dimensions?
decisive_failure: originality: ADMISSION_DEFECT: universal-convexity disproof was already published as DDP-W arXiv:2609.04675v1 (4 Sep 2026) ten days before the 14 Sep round, so Admission novelty screening was stale. Headline (a) is verbatim DDP-W Thm 1.1 (N>=8 one-parameter entire mean-convex nonconvex family); report explicitly claims no new construction, only assembled deduction, which is a mechanical implication of that prior theorem plus HIMW p.26 caveat. Under STANDARD a prior source substantively implying the claim defeats novelty even without verbatim headline; part (b) restates known HIMW/BLT18 status. Hence no new claim, boundary, or witness.

recovery_conditions: state a substantive result not covered by the identified prior work; address the recorded limitation: DDP-W arXiv:2609.04675 is a September 2026 preprint (v1); its 61-page construction is cited, not independently re-derived — if its proof were defective, part (a) reverts to conjectural.
